title: Remember highlighted menu item after returning from submenus
head: 7401a4a340f5
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Restoring after rows change can highlight an unselectable or nonexistent row
leads.consequence: If an extension's disabled: guard changes while its submenu is open, going back first runs rebuildDisplay/settleCursor (which skips disabled rows), then restoreSelection puts the cursor back on the saved row by ID without checking rowSelectable. The dimmed parent has selection styling even though Enter and clicks reject it. If all parent rows are removed or disabled, cursorActive becomes true despite no usable row. Preserve the saved ID only if selectable, otherwise run nextSelectable/settleCursor and leave cursorActive false for an empty menu.

leads.summary: Search drilldown drops the parent filter, so saved ID is absent and index restoration can select a different branch
leads.consequence: For example, search the root menu for 'font', select the nested style.font result and enter it. The saved itemId is style.font and its index is an index into the filtered search results. Back clears root.filterText and rebuilds only direct root children (apps, learn, trigger, style...), so no style.font row exists. restoreSelection clamps the filtered index into that unfiltered list, often selecting Apps instead of the Style branch and never restoring the search. Store the filter with the history or resolve the saved item's nearest visible parent row when returning to an unfiltered parent.

leads.summary: Direct submenu summons still return to the first parent row
leads.consequence: `omarchy menu summon style.font` opens without navStack or selectionStack. Left/Backspace uses goBack's no-history branch, opening Style with selectedIndex=0, not the Font row that was entered directly. The same happens for default bindings to named submenu routes. Consider selecting the previous submenu's row in the fallback branch (and its ancestor when needed).
leads.triage: corroborates Opus finding 5 (direct submenu route); published as Optional

leads.summary: Open menu-memory PR #12823 restores navStack but not the selection frames this PR requires
leads.consequence: #12823 remembers a menu's navStack on close and reuses it on a root summon within 15 seconds; this PR unconditionally clears selectionStack in openExistingMenu. If the two features are combined without restoring selection frames alongside the remembered history, Back in the reopened submenu pops a history menu but saved is null, so its parent highlight resets to the first selectable row; the same occurs for each older remembered history level. Their QML hunks also conflict and need an explicit integration, rather than simply keeping both independent changes.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator from sol/pr-12823.diff (openExistingMenu restores remembered navStack) and head Menu.qml:887; published as #12823 bullet; wording corrected per self-check F4

leads.summary: Seven other open PRs replace the same parent-selection/history flow with incompatible stack representations
leads.consequence: #13012, #12644, #13225, #7954, #12759, #11577 and #7074 independently edit setActiveMenu/goBack to push objects into navStack rather than the string IDs this PR pops, while this PR adds a second stack. All seven are diverged (none stacked), and merge-file against each own merge-base produces conflict markers in those functions. If the new object push is taken with this PR's string-based pop, setActiveMenu receives an object instead of an ID, falls back to root, and the saved.menu guard fails; tests in the competing PRs include regexes that also require different function signatures. Choose one history representation and reconcile the tests when merging either change.

leads.summary: Added test passes when restoreSelection is a no-op
leads.consequence: The only new assertion looks for three tokens in the QML source rather than exercising the functions. Prepending an unconditional `return` to restoreSelection while leaving all three tokens in place still passes the entire changed test under LC_ALL=C. Add a small navigation fixture that actually enters, changes the parent rows, returns, and checks selectedIndex/cursorActive, including disabled/empty and filter cases.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus finding 4 (test); published as Optional test improvement

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The main path works as described. After entering a submenu with the keyboard or a mouse click, Left/Backspace puts the cursor back on the row that was entered. This holds across nested levels and through link rows. Because the restore looks the row up by item ID, it still finds the right row when rows above it disappear while the submenu is open, where an index-only restore would not. Both open paths (`openExistingMenu` and `openDmenu`) reset `selectionStack` together with `navStack`. The PR applies cleanly to the current `quattro` tip, and `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` passes on the head and on the tip with the PR applied.

Two small edge cases, a test gap and an optional follow-up are below, plus a note on overlapping open PRs.

### Returning from a deeper search result can land on an unrelated row

Search rows include all descendants of the active menu, not only its direct children (`Menu.qml:625-650`). When a submenu is opened from a deeper result, the saved `itemId` is that deep ID and the saved `index` is its position in the *filtered* list. `goBack()` rebuilds the parent unfiltered, the deep ID is not a row there, and `restoreSelection()` falls back to the filtered index clamped into the unfiltered list (`Menu.qml:730-743`).

```text
root menu, type "style"     filtered list: [0] Style   [1] Install › Style
Down, Right                 enters install.style        saved { index: 1, itemId: "install.style" }
Left                        root list rebuilt unfiltered; "install.style" is not a root row
                            → index 1 → Learn           (base branch: Apps, row 0)
```

The same happens with `font` (Install › Style › Font at filtered index 1 → Learn). Results that are direct children of the parent restore correctly (`style` → Style).

**Impact:** After drilling into a deeper search result, going back highlights whichever parent row sits at that filtered position, usually unrelated to the path taken. The base branch at least lands predictably on the first row.

**Suggested change:** Before the index fallback, walk the saved ID up its `parent` chain until it matches a row of the menu being returned to, so Install › Style comes back to Install. The index fallback then only applies when the row really disappeared.

### The restore can put the cursor on a disabled row

`restoreSelection()` runs after `rebuildDisplay()` has already settled the cursor, then sets `selectedIndex` directly and forces `cursorActive = true` (`Menu.qml:743-744`). That skips the rule in `settleCursor()` (`Menu.qml:549-553`) and `docs/menu.md` that disabled rows are unselectable ("cursor, pointer, and Enter all step over it").

In a harness with a user-defined submenu row whose `disabled:` guard turns true while that submenu is open, Left leaves the cursor on the disabled row and Right does nothing. The base branch moves to the next selectable row. From the source, if the parent has no rows at all, `cursorActive` is still set to `true`.

**Impact:** Guards are re-evaluated only on open and on a menu-file reload, so the direct case needs a guard to flip while the submenu is open. The search fallback above could also land on a disabled row, but no case in the default menu was found where the restored row is disabled (every 1- and 2-letter search in Install was scanned with realistic guard states).

**Suggested change:** Replace the two assignments with `root.selectedIndex = restored; root.settleCursor()`. The saved `cursorActive` is then unnecessary: it is always `true` in practice, because entering a submenu requires an active cursor.

**Optional test improvement:** The new assertion (`test/shell.d/menu-test.sh:614-619`) only checks that three source strings exist. With `root.selectedIndex = restored` deleted, or with the ID lookup disabled, the full menu test still passes (128 ok on the tip with the PR applied). `docs/testing.md` ("Unit-testing shell JavaScript from bash") describes keeping plugin logic in `.js` modules so Node can test it. Moving the row resolution into `MenuModel.js` (for example a `restoredRowIndex(items, rowIds, saved)` helper, which needs the items map to walk parents) would allow real assertions: ID hit after rows shift, ancestor hit for a deep search result, clamped fallback, empty list and disabled row.

**Optional:** Menus opened directly on a submenu still return to the parent's first row, because they start with no history and `goBack()` takes the unchanged no-history branch (`Menu.qml:796-798`). For example, SUPER+ESCAPE opens System, and Left then highlights Apps rather than System. The same applies to SUPER+CTRL+C, SUPER+CTRL+O and SUPER+CTRL+H. Selecting the row whose ID equals the menu being left, in that branch, would cover it. The PR description says returning from a submenu "always highlighted the first row"; this path still does.

### Overlapping open PRs

Several open PRs implement the same "restore the row on back" behaviour: #7074, #7954, #11577, #12644, #12759, #13012 and #13225. On 2026-09-21 an Omarchy team member closed #7657, #7800 and #8322 as duplicates of #7074, asking any reopened PR to include "a note on the difference" ([example](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/7657#issuecomment-5758274855)). This PR was opened earlier and was not part of that sweep. `git merge-tree` reports a `Menu.qml` conflict between this PR and each of those seven PRs, and also #12823 (menu navigation memory).

- **Difference from #7074:** #7074 restores by index only. This PR restores by stable item ID, which keeps the right row when parent rows shift while the submenu is open.
- **#12823:** when the menu is reopened at the top level within a configurable window (15 seconds by default), it resumes the remembered submenu and its `navStack`, while this PR clears `selectionStack` in `openExistingMenu()`. If both land, the remembered history would also need its selection frames, or going back after a resumed open lands on the first row again.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head `7401a4a3`, plus isolated runs of `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` on the merge base, the head, the current `quattro` tip and the tip with the PR applied. Navigation behaviour was exercised with a Node harness that evaluates the real `Menu.qml` function bodies against the real default menu file, with a mocked list model and stubbed QML objects. Mutation checks were run on the test. No live Quickshell session was used, so rendering and scroll-into-view were not observed, and the author's manual check was not reproduced on a desktop. The disabled-row case used a synthetic user-defined menu. The related-PR search covered the newest 1000 open PRs by changed files plus keyword searches across all open PRs.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
